guitar.guitaristsText: Mick Ronson / Carlos Alomar / Earl Slick
guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul (Ronson) / Fender Stratocaster / Telecaster
guitar.notes: Bowie used many different guitarists across eras with no single signature instrument tied to Bowie himself; medium is appropriate given Ronson's well-known Les Paul.

tone.target: jangly chimey rock with slight chorus and airy reverb
tone.profile: jangly chimey rock with slight chorus and airy reverb
tone.summary: A bright, articulate signal chain featuring a light boost for accents, followed by a clean UK AC30-style amp model, enhanced with chorus and spring reverb to achieve the desired jangly, airy sound.

rig.name: David Bowie - China Girl - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle lift and brightness for arpeggiated accents without adding grit.
blocks.gap: The 'Boost' module is used to simulate a clean, transparent boost pedal (like an Overdrive set very low) rather than actual dirt.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone clean and articulate; no distortion needed.
Simulate the classic Vox AC30 chime and bright British tone.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the AC30 model.
blocks.gap: While 'UK Basket 4x12' might be more accurate for vintage Vox, 'UK Vintage 4x12' is used as the best available general bright UK cab option.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the bright mid-high frequencies and cut excessive low end for chime.
Add the required subtle, watery chorus effect for jangle.
Provide the airy, vintage reverb sound suggested by the source material.
Delay is not required and would clutter the clean arpeggios.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the vintage Vox AC30 sound and enhance chime.

proposals.reason: A dedicated 2x12 IR will better capture the vintage Vox/British sound and enhance chime.
